targetAudience.primary: Engineers designing resumable digital employees and human-in-the-loop agent workflows
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands agent context assembly, interruption and resume semantics.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A resumed agent can receive both a real operator response and regenerated context, yet ordinary message recency can make the synthetic event appear more authoritative.

whyNow: A same-day merged Google ADK change prevents workflow-wrapped single-turn agents from appending synthetic input when reconstructed resume inputs are present, exposing a precise evidence-ordering boundary.

externalHook.description: A newer synthetic event can be less authoritative than the older human response that actually resolves an interruption.

coreProposition: Resumable agent systems should preserve a monotonic, occurrence-scoped evidence order before model interpretation: once an operator response is reconstructed and admitted for a specific interruption, regenerated context must not silently outrank it, while identity, freshness and exactly-once effects remain separate controls.

originalValue.description: Reframes duplicate resume input as an authority-ordering failure and separates evidence continuity from operator authentication, approval freshness and downstream effect guarantees.

readerTakeaway: Attach interruption identity to resume evidence, resolve precedence before context assembly, and audit authorization and external effects independently of conversational ordering.

supported: ADK reconstructs known interrupt FunctionResponses into resume inputs.
The single-turn wrapper skips synthetic input injection when resume inputs are non-empty.
The regression test verifies the decisive guard with a representative resume-input mapping.
unsupported: Applicability to every agent resume path
uncertain: Whether unrelated resume inputs can suppress legitimate regeneration
How intentional supersession should be represented

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article develops a general resumable-agent evidence-ordering rule without relying on a first-party project.

decisionReason: The merged mechanism is concrete, the failure mode is consequential for HITL continuation, and the Research Object supports a transferable bounded control model.
